notes: Khubilai made Phagspa State Preceptor 1260 and Imperial Preceptor 1270, a patron-priest bond making Tibetan Buddhism the Yuan court faith; shamanic rites persisted. Mongols used Uyghur script before 1272. Jin population mixed Buddhist/Confucian/Daoist.

Coded the durable successor, the Roman aristocracy of the early Republic (Roman tradition). Porsena of Clusium (Etruscan religion) besieged or briefly held Rome, then withdrew. Latin inscriptions exist from the 7th-6th century BCE.

source1: Virginia Luling, Somali Sultanate: The Geledi City-State over 150 Years, Transaction Publishers 2002 - https://books.google.com/books?id=IqgEAAAACAAJ
notes: Geledi was a Sunni Muslim sultanate at Afgooye absorbed into Italian Somaliland c. 1908-1911. The Catholic Italian colonial state kept its own tradition; no adoption of Islam by the ruling group.

source1: R. Sathyanatha Aiyar, History of the Nayaks of Madura, Oxford University Press (Humphrey Milford) 1924 - http://archive.org/stream/in.ernet.dli.2015.183822/2015.183822.History-Of-The-Nayaks-Of-Madura_djvu.txt
notes: Aiyar: Chanda Sahib overthrew the Hindu cause and the last Nayak queen Minakshi c. 1736. Arcot was the capital of the Muslim nawabs, who remained Muslim and used Persian administration; no adoption.

source1: M. Arunachalam, The Kalabhras in the Pandiya Country, University of Madras 1979 - https://www.tamildigitallibrary.in/admin/assets/book/TVA_BOK_0019058_The_Kalabhras_in_the_Pandiya_country.pdf

notes: Kalabhras described as heterodox patrons of Jainism and Buddhism who seized Brahmin lands (Velvikudi grant); Arunachalam rejects Saiva claims, others assert them. Evidence scarce on later adoption and on elite literacy at conquest.

source1: George M. Moraes, The Kadamba Kula, B.X. Furtado and Sons 1931 - https://archive.org/stream/kadambakula035210mbp/kadambakula035210mbp_djvu.txt

notes: Kadambas a Brahman family devoted to Vedic study and sacrifice (Talagunda inscription), dispossessed by Chalukyas of Badami. Chalukyas built Brahmanical/Hindu temples at Badami and Pattadakal; both issued Sanskrit/Kannada inscriptions.

Italy's population was Catholic Christian (Gothic rulers Arian). Justinian's Chalcedonian Christian Byzantine empire waged war from 535 for nearly 20 years; Ostrogoths lost national existence after 554. Same tradition.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Treaty of Campo Formio - https://www.britannica.com/event/Treaty-of-Campo-Formio
notes: Catholic Venice fell to Napoleon 1797 and was ceded to Catholic Habsburg Austria by Campo Formio. The Directory was officially secular and anticlerical, but its elite and France were of Catholic Christian background; coded Christianity.
